Note: company is a QSR operator, so the chemicals subsector tag is a placeholder; see fields.

summary.headline: Westlife Foodworld Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% to INR7.47 billion, with same-store sales up 10.1% on double-digit guest count growth.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter in 13 quarters, with revenue up 16% YoY to INR7.47 billion and same-store sales growth of 10.1%, driven mainly by guest count growth that was double-digit in each month. Operating EBITDA rose 29% YoY (management also cited about 26% in one answer), with margin up 130 bps to 13.1% despite about 190 bps of inflation across commodities, utilities and employee costs. The company opened 11 restaurants, taking the network to 492 across 80 cities, and reiterated its 580+ restaurant target by March 2028. Management said momentum continued into October, and guided to 100-150 bps of annual profitability improvement and 2-4% price increases over the year.

segments.name: On-premise (dine-in)
segments.commentary: Grew 17% YoY in Q2 FY27, similar in pace to off-premise per management.

segments.name: Off-premise (delivery and takeaway)
segments.commentary: Grew 15% YoY; company says delivery is broad-based and in double-digit growth, with own-channel delivery trial in Mumbai.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Over 75% of sales; 58 million+ cumulative app downloads and about 4.2 million monthly active users.

guidance_outlook: Profitability: maintain 100-150 bps YoY margin improvement guidance for the year, excluding unforeseen shocks; management said the guidance holds despite Karnataka minimum wage increases and higher oil costs.
Pricing: 2-4% weighted average price increase over the year (around 3% typical), versus roughly 2% taken in each of the last couple of years; no large one-time hike planned.
Capex: total FY27 capex INR250-300 crore; per-store cost INR3-3.5 crore.
Expansion: 60-65 restaurants per year; 580+ restaurants by March 2028.
Trading: October momentum continued; management aspires to maintain high single-digit growth as a minimum, though it avoided formal forward-looking statements.
capex_capacity: Opened 11 restaurants in Q2 FY27, taking the total to 492 across 80 cities; 500th restaurant due the following week.
Plan of 60-65 new restaurants per year; target of 580+ by March 2028.
Capex per store INR3-3.5 crore; FY27 capex INR250-300 crore, with cost pressure from USD, duties and technology costs.
Own delivery rider fleet brought back in-house; Mumbai quick-delivery initiative to be scaled only after cost model is understood.
demand_pricing: Guest count grew double digits in each month of Q2; management says growth came from both new or returning customers (lapsed 6+ months) and higher frequency, per survey data.
Same-store sales growth of 10.1%; management said the 3% like-for-like average unit volume figure was a separate trailing-12-month data point and not comparable.
Value platform centred on INR99 entry meal, GMALite and partner discounts; management said discounting was reduced, not increased, and that no extra discount was given vs prior quarters.
Gap between South and West growth is narrowing per management, with strengthened South operating structure; IT-hub areas (Bangalore, Hyderabad) grew in line with West.
Inflation of about 190 bps across commodities, utilities and employee costs; management says price increases absorb roughly half of inflation as a principle.

qa_highlights.question: Promotional intensity and ad spend YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify; said value is a platform, discounting was reduced, and no extra discounts were given versus prior quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 3-4% price hike mean 190 bps of margin gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Not directly; price increases absorb about half of inflation, with cost-saving initiatives also in play, and guidance remains 100-150 bps annual margin improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Can the SSSG trajectory continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects value interventions and new consumer activations to keep guest count growth going, though it did not give a numeric forecast.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gap between SSSG and guest count closing, and what drives check size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guest count momentum since December is the priority; check size is easier to lift, and price contributed little from Q1 to Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Latika Chopra: Is 100-150 bps margin guidance applicable to FY27 given first-half gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management reaffirmed 100-150 bps for this year, citing Karnataka minimum wage hikes and oil costs but a mitigation plan and volume-led negotiating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 10% SSSG constructed, and what is capex per store and FY capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No further breakup of SSSG; per-store capex INR3-3.5 crore; FY27 capex INR250-300 crore rather than the INR300 crore figure floated.

risks_watch: Sustainability of double-digit guest count growth beyond the current festive season, given that management says value-led growth can fade over two or three quarters.
Input cost inflation: Karnataka minimum wage hike, edible oil and other commodities, and USD-linked capex costs.
Limited disclosure on promotional intensity and ad spend makes it hard to isolate the effect of value discounting on margins.
Delivery trajectory: own-channel delivery expansion beyond Mumbai pending cost model; SSSG split by channel not disclosed.
Restaurant rollout of 60-65 a year needs to hold to reach 580+ by March 2028.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on guest count and margins, but guarded on forward numbers and explicitly avoided quantifying promotions, SSSG breakdown and forward growth, citing a dynamic operating environment.
key_quotes: This quarter, we delivered our strongest performance in 13 quarters with double-digit growth in both guest count and same -store sales.
Most encouraging, guest count grew in double digits in each month of this quarter, demonstrating the strength of consumer demand and effectiveness of our brand plus value strategy.
So I'm quite confident that you will not see an adverse impact on gross margin from here on, unless and until there is something dramatically wrong, which goes on, which we cannot predict.
Value is easy. If you're going to get growth out of bill value, I think it lasts for two, three quarters and then fizzles.

financial_highlights.change: Double-digit; company says it is the quarter figure, not TTM
Up 130 bps YoY; EBITDA growth 29% YoY (one answer cites ~26%)

adds.what: Restaurant openings: 60-65 new restaurants per year, target 580+ by March 2028 (492 today, 11 opened in Q2 FY27)

growth.why: Management reiterated 60-65 openings a year and 580+ restaurants by March 2028 with FY27 capex of INR250-300 crore (INR3-3.5 crore per store), and held 100-150 bps margin expansion, backed by 11 openings in Q2 and a 2-4% price increase plan; high single-digit SSSG is an aspiration, not a formal forecast.
